title: 2013 HMMT November General Problem 7
statement: Find the largest real number \(\lambda\) such that \(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2} \geq a b+\lambda b c+c d\) for all real numbers \(a, b, c, d\).

solutions.text: \(\left.\begin{array}{|c}\frac{3}{2} \\ \text { Let } \\ \\ \hline\end{array} a, b, c, d\right)=\left(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}+d^{2}\right)-(a b+\lambda b c+c d)\). For fixed \((b, c, d), f\) is minimized at \(a=\frac{b}{2}\), and for fixed \((a, b, c), f\) is minimized at \(d=\frac{c}{2}\), so simply we want the largest \(\lambda\) such that \(f\left(\frac{b}{2}, b, c, \frac{c}{2}\right)=\frac{3}{4}\left(b^{2}+c^{2}\right)-\lambda b c\) is always nonnegative. By AM-GM, this holds if and only if \(\lambda \leq 2 \frac{3}{4}=\frac{3}{2}\).
